newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Spain's Santander bank increases Taiwan's presence.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Santander bank increases Taiwan's presence.

text.p: Spain's Banco Santander plans to upgrade its Taiwan office as part of a strategy to extend its foothold in the Far East, officials said on Thursday.

"We just teamed up last month the Taipei, Shanghai and Beijing offices with our Greater China headquarters in Hong Kong to concentrate our efforts in promoting business in the region," said Po-ling Cheung, the bank's Hong Kong branch public relations manager.
Santander, rated as the world's 33rd largest bank in terms of market capitalisation, is the number one bank both in Spain and Latin America.
Santigao Ruperez, the bank's Taipei office head, said his office, which opened in 1989, would play a more active role in Taiwan.
"We are increasing our presence in Taipei... and eventually we will upgrade our Taipei representative office to a full branch," Ruperez said.
"From now on, we will actively promote our image by hosting or taking part in various bank activities in Taiwan," he added.
Ruperez said the bank was scheduled to host a seminar on Friday to give an overall view of investment, including investment risk, in Latin America, where Taiwan has major diplomatic allies.
Santander Group is active in 32 countries with 5,170 offices and some 60,000 employees worldwide. At the end of March 1997, it posted record net income of US$260 million and assets of US$148 billion.
